title: 65. Numeracy & Number Systems: Order of Magnitude Comparisons
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Order of Magnitude in Scientific Notation
questions.learningObjective: Identify the order of magnitude of a number written in scientific notation.
questions.question: In this question, the order of magnitude of a positive number \(a\times10^n\), with \(1\le a<10\), means \(10^n\). Which number has an order of magnitude of \(10^4\)?
questions.explanation: The order of magnitude of a number in scientific notation is determined by its power of \(10\). The number \(4.3 \times 10^4\) has exponent \(4\), so its order of magnitude is \(10^4\). The number \(4.3 \times 10^3\) has exponent \(3\), so its order of magnitude is \(10^3\).
questions.hint: Look at the exponent of \(10\) in scientific notation.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize numbers that have the same order of magnitude.
questions.question: In this question, the order of magnitude of a positive number \(a\times10^n\), with \(1\le a<10\), means \(10^n\). Which number has the same order of magnitude as \(6 \times 10^7\)?
questions.explanation: Numbers have the same order of magnitude when they are written with the same power of \(10\) in scientific notation. The number \(6 \times 10^7\) has power \(10^7\), and \(4 \times 10^7\) also has power \(10^7\). Therefore, \(4 \times 10^7\) has the same order of magnitude as \(6 \times 10^7\). The alternative has order \(10^8\), which differs from the stated order \(10^7\).
questions.hint: Compare the exponents in scientific notation.

questions.learningObjective: Compare two numbers by examining their powers of 10.
questions.question: Which number is greater?
questions.explanation: Compare the powers of \(10\) first. The number \(2.5 \times 10^6\) has power \(10^6\), while \(7.8 \times 10^5\) has power \(10^5\). Since \(10^6 > 10^5\), the number \(2.5 \times 10^6\) is greater. For normalized positive scientific notation, a one-unit exponent difference cannot be reversed by coefficients between one and ten.
questions.hint: A larger exponent of \(10\) makes the number greater when comparing scientific notation.

questions.learningObjective: Determine which number has a larger order of magnitude.
questions.question: In this question, the order of magnitude of a positive number \(a\times10^n\), with \(1\le a<10\), means \(10^n\). Which number has a larger order of magnitude?
questions.explanation: The order of magnitude is determined by the power of \(10\). The number \(9.9 \times 10^3\) has order \(10^3\), while \(1.1 \times 10^4\) has order \(10^4\). Since \(10^4 > 10^3\), the number \(1.1 \times 10^4\) has a larger order of magnitude.
questions.hint: Compare the exponents, even if the coefficients are close in size.

questions.concept: Scaling a Number by a Power of Ten
questions.learningObjective: Determine the effect of multiplying a number by a power of ten.
questions.question: Which number is exactly \(100\) times \(4 \times 10^3\)?
questions.explanation:
Multiplying by \(100\) increases the exponent of \(10\) by \(2\):
\[
(4 \times 10^3) \times 100 = 4 \times 10^3 \times 10^2 = 4 \times 10^5
\]
Therefore, \(4 \times 10^5\) is exactly \(100\) times \(4 \times 10^3\). The alternative is only \(10\) times the given number, rather than \(100\) times.
questions.hint: Multiplying by \(100\) means increasing the power of \(10\) by \(2\).

questions.concept: Ratio of Numbers in Scientific Notation
questions.learningObjective: Calculate how many times larger one number is than another.
questions.question: How many times as large as \(4 \times 10^6\) is \(8 \times 10^8\)?
questions.explanation:
Divide the two numbers:
\[
\frac{8 \times 10^8}{4 \times 10^6}
= \frac{8}{4} \times 10^{8-6}
= 2 \times 10^2 = 200
\]
So \(8 \times 10^8\) is \(200\) times as large as \(4 \times 10^6\). The alternative is smaller by a factor of \(10\), owing to a misplaced exponent.
questions.hint: Divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the power of 10 closest to a given number.
questions.question: Which power of \(10\) is closest to \(9.7\times10^5\) in absolute numerical difference?
questions.explanation: The number \(9.7 \times 10^5\) equals \(970{,}000\). The nearby powers of \(10\) are \(10^5 = 100{,}000\) and \(10^6 = 1{,}000{,}000\). Since \(970{,}000\) is much closer to \(1{,}000{,}000\), the closest power of \(10\) is \(10^6\). The absolute differences are \(870{,}000\) from \(10^5\) and \(30{,}000\) from \(10^6\); this question asks for nearest numerical distance, rather than the scientific-notation exponent convention.
questions.hint: Convert the number to standard form and compare it with the nearby powers of \(10\).

questions.concept: Order of Magnitude for Small Numbers
questions.learningObjective: Determine the order of magnitude of a small decimal number.
questions.question: In this question, the order of magnitude of a positive number \(a\times10^n\), with \(1\le a<10\), means \(10^n\). Which number has the same order of magnitude as \(0.00042\)?
questions.explanation:
Write \(0.00042\) in scientific notation:
\[
0.00042 = 4.2 \times 10^{-4}
\]
Its order of magnitude is \(10^{-4}\). Therefore, \(4 \times 10^{-4}\) has the same order of magnitude. The alternative uses order \(10^{-3}\) instead of \(10^{-4}\).
questions.hint: Convert the decimal to scientific notation and compare the exponent.

questions.learningObjective: Determine how many times larger one scientific notation quantity is than another.
questions.question: How many times as large as \(5.0 \times 10^4\) is \(3.0 \times 10^7\)?
questions.explanation:
Divide the two numbers:
\[
\frac{3.0 \times 10^7}{5.0 \times 10^4}
= \frac{3.0}{5.0} \times 10^{7-4}
= 0.6 \times 10^3 = 600
\]
Thus, \(3.0 \times 10^7\) is \(600\) times as large as \(5.0 \times 10^4\). The alternative is smaller by a factor of \(10\), owing to a misplaced exponent.
questions.hint: Divide the coefficients and then handle the powers of \(10\).

questions.concept: Order of Magnitude Comparison in Context
questions.learningObjective: Compare two large distances by estimating their ratio.
questions.question: A light-year is about \(9.5 \times 10^{12}\text{ km}\). A distant object is about \(4.8 \times 10^{13}\text{ km}\) away. About how many times as large as one light-year is this distance?
questions.explanation:
Divide the distance by the length of a light-year:
\[
\frac{4.8 \times 10^{13}}{9.5 \times 10^{12}}
= \frac{4.8}{9.5} \times 10^{13-12}
\approx 0.5 \times 10 = 5
\]
Therefore, the distance is about \(5\) times as large as a light-year. The alternative is too large by a factor of \(10\), treating a one-unit exponent gap as a two-unit gap.
questions.hint: Divide the two numbers in scientific notation and estimate the coefficient.
